titre_chapitre: Balance Between Load and Production Capacity

questions.enonce: How is production capacity primarily measured and expressed for the purposes of this course?
options: In terms of the quantity of products manufactured[span_0](start_span)[span_0](end_span)
In terms of total electricity consumed per shift[span_1](start_span)[span_1](end_span)
In terms of total floor space in square meters[span_2](start_span)[span_2](end_span)
In terms of net profit margin per unit[span_3](start_span)[span_3](end_span)
questions.explication: Production capacity corresponds to the size of the operational production system and is expressed in terms of the quantity of products manufactured[span_4](start_span)[span_4](end_span).

questions.enonce: What is the general formula for workstation capacity ($C$) given operation time ($t$) and reference time unit ($U$)?
questions.explication: The capacity of a workstation expressed in product units is given by $C = U / t$, where $U$ is the reference time unit and $t$ is the operation time[span_9](start_span)[span_9](end_span).

questions.enonce: What action should be taken if there is too much dispersion in the measured times when timing an operation?
options: Identify and solve process dysfunctions, such as changing the method or station design[span_11](start_span)[span_11](end_span)
Multiply the times by the worker's experience factor[span_13](start_span)[span_13](end_span)
questions.explication: If there is too much dispersion in measurement times, it indicates a process dysfunction that needs to be identified and resolved rather than blindly taking an average[span_14](start_span)[span_14](end_span).
